questions.q:
What is the very first step in the scientific method?
A) Testing a guess
B) Observing something interesting
C) Giving up
D) Reading a textbook
questions.a: B) Observing something interesting. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks science starts with a pre-written answer rather than a genuine question sparked by observation.

questions.q: If you guess why a plant is dying, is that the end of the scientific process? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not the end. You must test your guess through observation or experiments to see if it is actually correct. A wrong answer shows the student ignores the "testing" phase, which is what separates a blind guess from science.

questions.q: Your friend says, "Science is only for people in white coats in labs." How do you use the scientific method to prove them wrong?
questions.a: Explain a daily example, like a bicycle repair person finding a flat tire leak. By checking the tire (observation), guessing it's a puncture (hypothesis), and putting it in water to see bubbles (testing), they are performing the scientific method. A wrong answer indicates the student hasn't connected scientific steps to non-lab environments.

questions.q: Why do we call science an "unending jigsaw puzzle"?
questions.a: Because every new discovery creates more questions, and sometimes we have to rearrange our previous knowledge if a new piece (discovery) doesn't fit. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks science is "finished" or static, rather than an evolving process.

questions.q: Is it better to do science alone or with others? Justify your choice based on the nature of science.
questions.a: Working with others is often better because science is rarely a solitary task; team members can share observations and help solve problems faster. A wrong answer shows a lack of understanding that scientific inquiry thrives on collaboration and shared curiosity.

questions.q: Think of a kitchen mystery (like why milk spills when boiled). Describe how you would investigate this using the scientific method.
questions.a: The student should identify the observation (milk spilling), form a hypothesis (too high heat or full pot), test it by changing one factor (e.g., using a larger pot or lower heat), and observe the result. A poor answer lacks the structured "test" step.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Science is a systematic way of observing our ______, asking questions about how things work, and using a step-by-step method to find logical answers.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why your pen suddenly stopped writing even though it ______ full of ink?
What is Science? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Science is a systematic way of observing our surroundings, asking questions about how things work, and using a step-by-step method to find logical answers.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Science?
questions.a: Students often believe that if their "guess" (hypothesis) turns out to be wrong, they have failed at science.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify the steps of the scientific method in a real-life situation and explain how curiosity drives the process of discovery.
